newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile turns torture center into Park of Peace.
newsitem.headline: Chile turns torture center into Park of Peace.

text.p: The largest torture centre under Gen. Augusto Pinochet's military regime opened as a Park of Peace on Saturday as a tribute to the victims of the dictatorship that gripped Chile from 1973 to 1990.
The park was inaugurated on a site known as Villa Grimaldi, which the military regime named Fort Terra Nova and where nearly 5,000 mainly left-wing activists were imprisoned and treated brutally.

"This is the first monument for the victims in the struggle for social justice", Maria Isabel Ortega, a former leftist leader who spent a month in the fort that operated as a torture centre from 1974 to 1978, told the opening ceremony.

Ortega said the park was the first former torture centre in Latin America to be turned into a tribute to its victims. A similar site in Uruguay is now a shopping mall, and one in Argentina is a parking lot.
Relatives of the 223 people who were executed or who disappeared in the centre laid carnations by a wall bearing the victims' names.
The relatives, mostly women, wept as they identified the names of their lost loved ones on the wall.

"To the people whose names are on the wall, to their relatives, we want to say that their suffering was not in vain, that their memory enlightens our spirit and our actions", Chilean minister of Housing Edmundo Hermosilla told the gathering.

He stressed Chile should never forget what happened under Pinochet. "Do not believe those who say this (the torture) never happened. This park is for them, but also for us, to make sure it will never happen again", Hermosilla said.
Pinochet stepped down as the country's ruler in 1990, but still leads the army as its commander-in-chief and cannot be removed until 1998 under Chile's constitution, which he passed.

Under his regime about 3,000 people were killed and/or disappeared, and about 50,000 were exiled, according to an independent report commissioned by the government after democracy was re-established in 1990.
